title: Silver usage grain: defensive casts + healthstone/potion usage events
description:
## Why

`silver.defensive_buff_window` captures aura windows but cannot answer "what was used": healthstone/potion usage isn't captured at all, and cast events are the ground truth needed for cooldown inference. Aura windows alone also miss instant/absorb-style usages.

## Acceptance criteria

* New silver projection (e.g. `silver.survival_action`) with one row per defensive/healthstone/potion use per player per encounter: timestamp ms into fight, cast spell ID, kind/category, and heal amount + overheal for consumable heals (join `SPELL_CAST_SUCCESS` with the resulting `SPELL_HEAL`).
* Gated by the game-data catalog — this must not become a generic cast warehouse (silver layer boundary rule).
* Rebuildable per encounter like other silver projections, keyed on `encounter_dim_id`.
* Tests cover a real-log fixture containing at least one healthstone or potion use and one defensive cast; current-tier potion spell IDs are resolved from observed real-log events, not memory.

title: Retail-current defensive & consumable catalog with cooldown/talent metadata
description:
## Why

The raid lead's #1 question set for the deployed mirror is "Defensives. And rocks/pots." The existing `WeGoNext.GameData.DefensiveBuffs` catalog is aura-IDs only — no cast IDs, no cooldown durations, no class/spec/talent mapping, no healthstones/potions — and is unverified against current retail (Midnight 12.x). Availability inference ("was it on cooldown when they died?") needs cooldown/charge metadata; "what was talented" needs talent association.

## Acceptance criteria

* Game-data catalog covers personal defensives per class/spec for **current retail**, plus Healthstone and current-tier health potions. Each entry carries: cast spell ID, aura spell ID(s), base cooldown, charges where relevant, category (personal/external/immunity/consumable), and talent association where the ability is talent-gated.
* Spell IDs are verified against observed events in imported retail logs (or retail-only references) — **no MoP-Classic/Classic/other-flavor IDs**. DBM ships multi-flavor mods; do not source IDs from them blindly. Where an ID cannot be confirmed, it stays out rather than guessed in.
* Consumables model the shared potion cooldown and per-combat usage constraints so availability inference is possible downstream.
* Catalog stays plain data tables gating silver projection (same pattern as `DefensiveBuffs` today); existing duplicate/suspect entries (e.g. double Fortifying Brew IDs, Mirror Image) are audited.

Initiative: `docs/initiatives/07-defensives-and-consumables.md`.

title: Feign Death is counted as a death in silver.death
description:
UNIT_DIED carries a trailing unconsciousOnDeath flag. Feign Death logs UNIT_DIED with flag 1; real deaths log 0. Nothing in the Zig parser or the silver projector reads it, so every hunter feign becomes a silver.death row.

Evidence (Sept 6 log, combat_log_files id 30): only Mädz (BM hunter) ever logs flag 1, 10 times; every other player's UNIT_DIED lines carry 0. On Sszorak pull 5 (gold 440), Mädz's 0:20.5 and 1:32 "deaths" are flag-1 feigns (Mädz keeps casting afterwards, with no resurrection); the real death is 2:51. The real first death on that pull is Kahnu at 2:35 (Mutilate).

Found by the Analysis layer: the Opus 5.5 baseline run (we-xf4.8) inferred Feign Death on Q1/Q4 from post-death casts and the judge flagged it. The live Q1 session and the Q1/Q4 reference answers both named the feign as the first death.

Impact: death counts, first-death and death-recap read models, survival/defensive analysis (Q5/Q6/Q10), and Analysis Tools `deaths` / `log_events` consumers.

Done when: the parser emits the flag, silver excludes flagged rows from deaths (or marks them), the death derivation stamp is bumped, the Sept 6 log rebuilds with Mädz's pull-440 deaths reduced from 3 to 1, and a real-log test covers a feign line. Then re-version reference answers Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4/Q5/Q6/Q10 against the rebuilt silver. Medallion change: ask-first under the phase 1 spec.

title: Death-window survival analysis: died-through / available-but-unused / on-cooldown
description:
## Why

The coaching question at every death: did they use anything, did they die *through* a pot or defensive (used it and died anyway), and what was sitting available — including rocks/pots?

## Acceptance criteria

* For each `silver.death`, a derived read model (gold/document-section input) reporting:
  * survival actions used within the death window (configurable, default ~10s before death),
  * actions active at the moment of death → "died through X",
  * catalog defensives that were talented and off cooldown at death → "available but unused",
  * healthstone/potion availability at death (shared potion cooldown state, healthstone usage).
* Cooldown availability is inferred (last use + base cooldown; encounter-start state unknown) and the read model labels it as inference (e.g. "likely available"), not asserted fact.
* Tests against real or fixture deaths covering at least: one "died with defensive available" case and one "died through a pot/defensive" case.

title: AI analysis phase 1: Tools over MCP
description:
Spec: docs/specs/ai-analysis-phase1.md (decisions and verification plan live there). Decision map: we-c5q.

## Goal

Let the operator run real Analysis sessions from Claude Code over the logs on file. Claude Code calls our starter Tools through a dev-only MCP endpoint, and every Tool call and verdict is recorded so retros can find promotions.

## Why

The operator wants analysis to grow through use: an expensive model explores early in a raid tier, operations it repeats get promoted into Tools and Playbooks, and later sessions get cheaper and more automated. Phase 1 is the cheapest way to start collecting that usage. Claude Code is the chat, so no session UI or API client is needed before real sessions exist. Success for the operator is asking the 12 corpus questions (`docs/ai-analysis/question-corpus.md`) about the Sept 6 raid between or after pulls and getting cited answers, with a record good enough to review afterwards.

## Non-goals

- The in-app agent loop, Anthropic API client, LiveView session screen, and spend-cap enforcement (phase 2; decisions locked on the map).
- Composite Tools (pull comparison, unruled-spell ranking, coaching notes). They must emerge through Promotion. Shipping them now defeats the point.
- Auto-runs, in-app retro, DB-backed Playbooks, model routing (Jev), name aliasing.
- Any exposure beyond the operator's machine: no public mirror, no raider access.
- Initiative 7's defensive/consumable silver grain. `log_events` stands in for it.
- Anti-goal: Tools that write anything, or that turn silver into a generic raw-event warehouse.

## Acceptance checks

1. **End to end, outside the code.** In Claude Code, the operator connects to the MCP endpoint, starts the `analysis-session` prompt and asks corpus Q1 about a Sszorak pull from Sept 6. The answer cites Tool evidence for every factual claim, and each Tool call it made appears as a row in the `analysis` Tool-call table.
2. **All 11 Tools listed over MCP** (7 starter plus 4 session-support), each with passing tests per the verification plan.
3. **Size cap holds.** On the largest real pull (Twin Fangs, about 107 MB, 368k events), every starter Tool's result stays at or under the cap, or truncates with a usable cursor.
4. **`log_events` speed.** A filtered `log_events` call on that pull returns in at most 0.5 s on the ReleaseSafe build, from local disk. Baseline: 1.04–1.34 s unfiltered ReleaseSafe and 2.2–3.9 s Debug (we-c5q.3).
5. **Read-only and loopback-only are enforced.** A test shows a Tool attempting a write fails inside its read-only transaction, and an MCP request from a non-loopback address is rejected.
6. **Verdicts land.** Saying "that's wrong, it was X" in a session produces a structured verdict row linked to the session.
7. **Export works.** Exporting a real session yields JSONL in which each Tool call from the transcript is matched to its server-side row.
8. **Reference set.** All 12 reference answers are checked in and operator-verified. One graded run of the 12 questions is recorded as the baseline score; phase 1 sets no pass threshold.
9. **Medallion untouched.** No silver, gold or rules schema changes. Import behaviour of `parse_events/4` is unchanged: existing import and silver tests pass.
10. **Gates.** `mix test` (feature tests need a working chromedriver), `mix credo`, `mix format`, zero compile warnings.

## Ask-first boundaries

- Adding any dependency other than a single MCP server library, or upgrading Req.
- Any change to silver, gold or rules schemas or projections, or to `parse_events/4` behaviour.
- Any write path from a Tool, or binding the endpoint beyond localhost or outside dev.

title: What is the contract every Tool follows?
description:
## Question

What shape does every Tool have?

- Definition: name, description for the model, input schema, and where Tools live in the codebase (likely their own context over the medallion, not inside silver/gold).
- Results: size bounds, truncation and pagination, and how results reference evidence (encounter, pull, timestamps, log byte offsets) so answers can cite them.
- Guarantees: read-only, deterministic for the same inputs, time limits.
- Testing: how a Tool is tested against real-log fixtures.
close_reason: WeGoNext.Analysis, module per Tool + registry; {data, evidence, truncated, next_cursor} ~8 KB; real names; read-only/deterministic/5 s/is_error; real-log fixture tests

comments.author: Ryan Messner
comments.text:
Resolution (grilling via foreman requests, 2026-10-29); all five recommendations accepted.
1. Home: new WeGoNext.Analysis context (lib/we_go_next/analysis/), one module per Tool implementing a behaviour (name/0, description/0, input_schema/0 as JSON schema, run/2 with args and session context). A registry module lists enabled Tools as data. Tools call existing silver/gold/document/bronze read functions and never own tables.
2. Result envelope: JSON {data, evidence, truncated, next_cursor}. Evidence names each row's source (pull id, timestamps, byte offset for log_events). Cap about 8 KB; over the cap, truncate with a cursor.
3. Real character names go to the model (no aliasing). Revisit only if the guild objects.
4. Read-only DB transaction, no file writes; deterministic for the same inputs and data; 5 s limit per call; errors and timeouts return to the model as is_error, never crash the session.
5. Tests: DataCase over real-log fixture slices asserting envelope and evidence; schema test for agent args; size test on the largest real pull; timing assertion for log_events on the Twin Fangs fixture.

title: Where does the agent loop run, and are Tools also exposed over MCP?

title: Which provider, client and model options fit a tool-using agent loop in Phoenix?
description:
## Question

What are the options for running a tool-use agent loop from Elixir/Phoenix, and what do they cost?

- Provider APIs with tool use and streaming (Anthropic Messages API first; note others only for comparison): tool-call protocol, streaming events, prompt caching, context limits, current model ids and per-token pricing.
- Elixir clients: Req directly vs existing libraries (e.g. anthropix, langchain for Elixir); maturity, streaming support, tool-call support.
- Streaming into LiveView and running tool calls in supervised BEAM processes.
- Rough cost per Analysis session for a plausible session shape (N turns, M tool calls, result sizes), per model tier.
- Data handling: what leaves the machine (player names, guild logs) and the provider's retention terms.

Findings feed the agent-runtime and model-tier decisions.
close_reason: Anthropic API via Req, session GenServer + PubSub; cached session ~$0.84 Opus / $0.42 Sonnet / $0.03 Haiku; caching mandatory

comments.author: Ryan Messner
comments.text:
Resolution (research, 2026-10-29). Detail: docs/research/llm-agent-provider-options.md on local branch research/llm-provider-options (1d811cc).

- Recommended: Anthropic Messages API via plain Req (repo is on Req 0.5; req_llm needs Req >= 0.6; langchain is mature but brings its own framework; anthropix stale). Small SSE parser needed for streaming.
- Process shape: one GenServer per Analysis session under a DynamicSupervisor, PubSub to LiveView, Tool calls under Task.Supervisor with timeouts, Tool failures returned as is_error.
- Pricing per MTok in/out: Fable 5.1 10/50, Opus 5.5 4/20, Sonnet 5.5 2/10, Haiku 5.5 0.10/0.50 (5x over 100K-token prompts). 1M context. Cache reads 0.05x (Opus/Sonnet).
- Modelled session (8 turns, 20 tool calls, 15 KB prefix, 6 KB results): cached ~$0.84 Opus, ~$0.42 Sonnet, ~$0.03 Haiku; uncached about 5x more. Prompt caching is mandatory; prefer the 1-hour TTL because operators reply slowly between pulls. Switching model mid-session drops the cache.
- Data: Tool results leave the machine (character names, GUIDs). Anthropic does not train on API traffic by default; 30-day retention. Aliasing names per session is an option for the Tool contract ticket.
- TypeSafe Jev: callable from Req at its typed-decision endpoint, $0.042/M input (vendor), US-hosted. Jev Router via OpenRouter is a poor fit (loses Anthropic caching); direct Jev is a later option for Tool/Playbook selection and confidence-gated escalation.
- Unconfirmed: some Anthropic details came from a cached reference (2026-10-06); the cost model's tokens-per-byte and output sizes are assumptions.

title: How can Tools read bronze, silver and gold fast enough over 1GB+ logs?
description:
## Question

What read paths exist today, and what is missing, for Tools to answer agent queries in interactive time over real logs (the Sept 6 log is about 1.17 GB)?

- Bronze: `LogReader` byte offsets, encounter boundaries, the Zig NIF parser. Can a Tool re-parse one encounter's byte range on demand, and how long does that take on a real pull? Is there an index from encounter/pull to byte range?
- Silver/gold: which projections and facts already answer common questions (damage taken events, deaths, debuffs, interrupts, damage done, fact_failure)?
- What a Tool needs that no layer has (e.g. raw event slices filtered by unit/spell/time window) and the cheapest way to provide it without turning silver into a generic raw-event warehouse.
- Measured timings on a real log, not estimates.

This is local-codebase research: read the code, benchmark on a real log, report numbers.
close_reason: Silver/gold answer most families in ms; anything else = filtered bronze re-parse of one pull (~0.2 s with in-NIF filter); NIF needs ReleaseSafe + dirty scheduler

comments.author: Ryan Messner
comments.text:
Resolution (research, 2026-10-29, all numbers measured). Detail: docs/research/tool-read-paths.md + docs/research/scripts/ on local branch research/tool-read-paths (1c748f7).

- Byte-range index already exists: gold.dim_encounter and public.encounters carry start_byte/end_byte; lookup 0.05 ms; parse_events/4 re-parses one pull on demand. (No LogReader module exists; the AGENTS.md listing is stale.)
- Bronze re-parse of the largest pull (Twin Fangs, 106.7 MB, 368k events): 2.2-3.9 s on the dev Debug NIF build, 1.0-1.3 s ReleaseSafe on local disk, 1.4-1.75 s from /mnt/e. Median pull ~0.6 s ReleaseSafe. One parsed pull is ~200 MB BEAM heap: caching parsed pulls is not viable.
- In-NIF substring prefilter prototype: largest pull 0.14-0.21 s and 7-9 MB result. The parse, not Elixir filtering, is the cost.
- Recomputing silver at Tool time is not viable (3.7-4.8 s per pull).
- Silver/gold are interactive: single-pull queries 0.03-1.7 ms; one spell across 26 pulls 18-20 ms; one player across all pulls 63-66 ms (seq scan); encounter document read 8-18 ms per MB.
- Read path per question family: pull summary -> encounter document; failures -> gold.fact_failure; deaths/hits/debuffs/damage done/casts -> silver tables; anything else (heals, buffs, resources, raw event slices) -> filtered bronze re-parse scoped to one pull.
- Prerequisites: ReleaseSafe + dirty_cpu NIF, a filtered parse entry point, Tool bronze reads from local disk, a resolver for moved archive paths (10/29 combat_log_files paths stale).
- Not measured: typed field-level NIF filters, dirty-scheduler behaviour under LiveView load, truly cold /mnt/e, Sept 6 silver/gold (that log is not imported).

title: AI analysis layer: LLM agent over the logs, growing its Tools through use
description:
## Destination

An approved spec, split into build tickets, for phase 1: the starter Tools in a WeGoNext.Analysis context, exposed over a dev-only MCP endpoint so real Analysis sessions run from Claude Code, with the Tool-call log, record_verdict, analyst instructions, Playbooks and the Sept 6 reference set. Plus the locked phase 2 decisions (in-app loop, tiers, caps, analysis schema) that the phase 1 build must not contradict. (Redrawn 2026-10-29: the phase 2 session screen is prototyped after phase 1 has real sessions.)

## Notes

- Vocabulary: `GLOSSARY.md` (Analysis session, Tool, Playbook, Auto-run, Promotion, Retro). Every session uses these terms.
- Charting decisions (2026-10-29, with the operator):
  - Local operator only. The first slice is driven by chat; context-driven Auto-runs come after Tools are built out through use.
  - The layer sits on top of the medallion: Tools read bronze, silver and gold. The medallion stays the reproducible source of truth.
  - Promotion targets are Tool (code), Playbook (data), Auto-run and medallion output. Only Tool and Playbook are designed in this map.
  - Retro proposes promotions and the operator approves them. Tool code lands as normal reviewed repo changes. The in-app agent never writes or runs generated code. Playbooks are stored data.
  - First retros run outside the app (Claude Code over exported session records, like `/retro`). An in-app retro comes later.
- Skills: grilling and domain-modeling for decisions; research, prototype; ui-patterns and ux-critique for session UI.
- Respect the medallion layer boundaries in `AGENTS.md`. Never reintroduce legacy analyzer-cache or `public.mechanic_criteria` surfaces.

## Decisions so far

- [Which provider, client and model options fit a tool-using agent loop in Phoenix? (we-c5q.2)](we-c5q.2): Anthropic Messages API over plain Req, a supervised session process streaming to LiveView; prompt caching mandatory (cached session roughly $0.84 Opus, $0.42 Sonnet, $0.03 Haiku); Jev only later, called directly.
- [How can Tools read bronze, silver and gold fast enough over 1GB+ logs? (we-c5q.3)](we-c5q.3): silver/gold answer most question families in milliseconds; everything else is a filtered bronze re-parse of one pull (about 0.2 s with an in-NIF filter, about 1 s without), never a cached parsed pull or Tool-time silver recompute.
- [Which real questions must the first slice answer? (we-c5q.1)](we-c5q.1): 12 questions across wipes, deaths, mechanics, coaching and own play (docs/ai-analysis/question-corpus.md); a third are cross-pull, two need Initiative 7's defensive grain.
- [What starter Tools does the first slice ship? (we-c5q.6)](we-c5q.6): primitives only, one per layer read (list_pulls, pull_summary, deaths, failures, damage_taken, interrupts, log_events); composites are left to emerge through Promotion; raw log_events ships before Initiative 7.
- [What is the contract every Tool follows? (we-c5q.7)](we-c5q.7): WeGoNext.Analysis context, one module per Tool plus a registry; result envelope {data, evidence, truncated, next_cursor} capped near 8 KB; real names; read-only, deterministic, 5 s, errors back to the model; real-log fixture tests.
- [Where does the agent loop run, and are Tools also exposed over MCP? (we-c5q.4)](we-c5q.4): MCP first so Claude Code drives real sessions early; then a GenServer-per-session in-app loop over Req; 40 requests, 10 minutes, cancel.
- [What should each model tier cost, and when does the season policy switch tiers? (we-c5q.5)](we-c5q.5): Opus 5.5 first, fixed per session by operator choice; $5 per session and $50 per night caps; automatic switching stays in the fog.
- [What does the agent know up front when a session starts? (we-c5q.8)](we-c5q.8): one set of analyst instructions in priv/analysis/ (MCP prompt now, system prompt later); a 2-3 KB active-log snapshot; boss plus global Playbooks auto-load, others via Tools.
- [How do answers cite log evidence, and how do we check they are right? (we-c5q.10)](we-c5q.10): every claim cites Tool evidence or is marked inference; a 12-question reference set on the Sept 6 log is rerun after changes; verdicts are structured data.
- [What does an Analysis session record keep so a retro can find promotions? (we-c5q.11)](we-c5q.11): transcript plus server-side Tool-call log in phase 1; an 'analysis' schema kept indefinitely; one JSONL export for retros and training.
- [How are Playbooks stored, scoped and loaded into a session? (we-c5q.9)](we-c5q.9): Markdown in priv/analysis/playbooks/ under git; front-matter scope by boss and question family; created only from approved retros, retired not deleted, version recorded per session.

## Not yet specified

- Phase 2 session screen: its ticket stays open and waits on real phase 1 sessions, then resolves by prototype.

- Auto-run: which log-state changes (new pull, encounter end, import finished) trigger which Tools, and how results reach the session.
- Medallion promotion rung: when an Auto-run is stable enough to become a deterministic silver/gold/document output, and who decides.
- In-app Retro: moving the out-of-app retro into the product (session browser, promotion proposals, approval flow).
- Season policy automation: switching model tiers automatically as Tool coverage grows (depends on the tier policy decision).
- Routed selection (roadmap): a typed-decision router model such as TypeSafe Jev picks the model and reasoning effort per request, and later which Tools to call or Auto-run. Early access since 2026-09-15; vendor-reported pricing and accuracy unverified.
- Evaluation over time: measuring whether promotions actually make sessions cheaper and answers better across a tier.

## Out of scope

- Raider-facing or public-mirror access to Analysis sessions (local operator only).
- Training our own models on past logs and session records (a later effort; this map only keeps the data usable for it, see the session record ticket).

title: Attribute pet and guardian damage done to owning players
description:
## Why
silver.damage_done dropped all pet/guardian damage (source GUID is the pet, not a Player-), undercounting pet specs (Demonology, BM, WW Xuen, etc.).

## Acceptance criteria
- Parser NIF emits owner_guid from the advanced block only when infoGUID == source GUID and owner is a Player- GUID (pet melee lines).
- Projector builds a full-pass pet->owner map from SPELL_SUMMON and swing ownerGUID, and attributes pet/guardian damage to the owner.
- Real-log fixture test (Twin Fangs pull, felguard + Imp Lord) covers both evidence paths.

description:
